We've covered several stories about Apple Vision Pro being used in healthcare settings. This week, Stryker announced that the first surgical procedure using a new app on Vision Pro has been completed.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, performed using the SportSuite Vision app, which brings "critical digital content into the surgeon's spatial environment," including arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scans.

Here's how Stryker describes the app:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's field of view, allowing them to see both physical objects and digital tools simultaneously in the operating room, including arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scans. During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons often rely on multiple displays in the operating room to view imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's line of sight, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional monitors and support a more streamlined, ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. According to Stryker, this is the first app authorized by the FDA to be used during surgical procedures on Vision Pro.

Separately, Pfizer also announced this week that it is using Apple Vision Pro to "create a memorable immersive experience" to "showcase" its determination to "conquer cancer."

You can learn more about the experience on Groove Jones's website.
